attempts.summary: Built the required double-NAT path: node3 (lan-a, 10.10.1.12) opens TCP connections to node4's HTTP service on port 8080 (lan-b, 10.10.3.13). node1 (VyOS) source-NATs traffic entering the transit network (masquerade to its eth1 address 10.10.2.1) via `nat source rule 100`. node2 (OPNsense) source-NATs traffic entering lan-b via automatic outbound NAT on vtnet2 (masquerade to its lan-b address 10.10.3.254). node4 records the connection as arriving from 10.10.3.254 (node2), never seeing node3's or node1's real address — confirmed via curl and packet captures at every hop (lan-a, transit, lan-b). Interface-to-NIC mapping was discovered empirically via ARP/STP probing since node1 (VyOS, 3 NICs) and node2 (OPNsense, 3 NICs) needed correct pairing with node3/node4's second NICs. Ran the full mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot-identity baselines on all 4 nodes, restarted them one at a time (node1 VyOS reboot, node2 OPNsense shutdown -r, node3/node4 Ubuntu sudo reboot), confirmed changed boot identity on each (boot_id for Linux nodes, kern.boottime for FreeBSD), and re-verified the double-NAT chain end-to-end and per-hop after each restart and after all four restarts completed. All configuration (VyOS config.boot via save, OPNsense config.xml, Ubuntu /etc/network/interfaces.d static configs) persisted correctly across reboots; only the ephemeral test HTTP server on node4 (running from /tmp) needed manual restart after its reboot, which was done and re-verified.
